title: Osteomyelitis, lupus and blistering skin disease
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for systemic lupus erythematosus and renal involvement.

HPI
The patient is a 67-year-old male presenting today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his systemic lupus erythematosus. He is currently managed on mycophenolate mofetil for the treatment of his lupus nephritis. He reports that he has been feeling generally stable over the last month. He denies any new-onset joint pain, significant fatigue, or new rashes. He notes that he has been adherent to his medication regimen and has not experienced any significant gastrointestinal side effects or acute infections. He reports that his urine output has remained consistent and he denies any visible hematuria or foamy urine.

Review of Systems
The patient denies fever, chills, weight loss, or night sweats. He denies chest pain or shortness of breath. He denies any new joint swelling or morning stiffness. He denies any neurological symptoms such as numbness or tingling. He denies any changes in vision or hearing.

Social History
The patient is a retired professional who lives with his spouse. He reports no tobacco or alcohol use. He enjoys walking and gardening as his primary forms of exercise.

Family History
His father had hypertension and his mother had a history of autoimmune disease.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Weight: 195 lbs

Recent Labs
Serum Creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL
eGFR: 52 mL/min/1.73m2
Urinalysis: Trace protein, no RBCs.
Complete Blood Count (CBC): Within normal limits.

Medication List
Mycophenolate mofetil 1000mg twice daily
Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily
Calcium carbonate 500mg daily

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is clear without new lesions or rashes. No joint swelling or erythema noted upon palpation of the hands or knees. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs.

Assessment
1. Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
2. Lupus nephritis (glomerular disease)

Plan
1. Continue mycophenolate mofetil 1000mg twice daily.
2. Continue current blood pressure medications.
3. Monitor renal function and urinalysis every 3 months.
4. Patient instructed to report any new symptoms of fatigue or changes in urine output immediately.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Glomerular disease in systemic lupus erythematosus: M32.14 (HCC 94).
